subject: Re: Payment schedule and Net-90 exception request for multi-year prepay
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@quantaflow.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Payment options for multi-year commitment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo — the team liked Redwood's latency profile. We are moving toward a multi-year commitment but procurement has pushed back on full upfront prepay. They have asked whether we can do: a 50% upfront prepay for year 1, then milestone-based invoices (3 equal milestones across year 2), and standard Net 90 terms on the milestone invoices.

They're also requesting a 10% term discount if we sign a 3-year commit (annual billing schedule to be aligned with our fiscal year). Can Redwood agree to Net 90 on milestone invoices if we take the 3-year term discount and keep some portion prepaid?

Attached is our internal procurement checklist (redacted).

Thanks,
Elena
Procurement Manager
Quantaflow

Attachments: Quantaflow_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (pdf)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@quantaflow.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment options for multi-year commitment

Hi Elena — appreciate the transparency. Short answer: we can be flexible, but we need to align on economics and risk. A few quick options that could work: 

1) 3-year prepay with 10% term discount, 50% upfront (year 1), remaining 50% split into two milestone invoices in year 2 and year 3; milestone invoices Net 90. Redwood would require a modest credit/security hold on milestone invoices until paid (standard).

2) 2-year commitment with 25% discount, 30% upfront, annual billing thereafter with Net 60 on annual invoices (less preferred).

3) Hybrid: 36-month term, 20% upfront, 40% prepaid applied across first 12 months, then milestone invoices for usage overages with Net 90.

I attached a proposed term schedule (v2) showing pricing, ramp, and the cap on overage rates. If you can confirm which structure procurement prefers, I’ll loop in finance (Ben) to validate credit and security language.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Term_Schedule_v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Payment options for multi-year commitment — finance input

So — quick notes from finance:

- Net 90 is higher risk; if we accept Net 90 on milestone invoices we should require either (a) 50% upfront or (b) an irrevocable bank guarantee / letter of credit for the milestone amounts.
- For a 10% term discount on a 3-year prepay, we need 60% of total value secured upfront (can be combination of cash + LC).
- Recommend approving the 50% upfront + milestone Net 90 with LC for milestones, or accept 30% upfront + shorter Net terms (Net 60) if customer cannot provide LC.

If procurement is firm on Net 90 with no LC we should not take the 10% discount.

-Ben
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@quantaflow.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@quantaflow.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment options for multi-year commitment

Thanks Soojin — I had a call with procurement this morning. Their constraints: they cannot issue an LC. For budget reasons they prefer Net 90 on milestone invoices. They are comfortable with 50% upfront in cash.

They also asked whether Redwood can stagger the milestone schedule so milestones align to product deliverables (ramp milestones at 9 months and 21 months) rather than fixed calendar anniversaries. Finally, they asked whether the 10% term discount could be conditioned on a revenue ramp schedule (i.e., minimum committed consumption per year).

Can Redwood confirm acceptance of: 3-year term, 10% term discount, 50% upfront, milestones at 9/21 months with Net 90 on milestone invoices (no LC)?

Best,
Elena
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@quantaflow.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment options for multi-year commitment

Elena — thanks for the clarity. We want to get this across the finish line. Final position from Redwood: 

- We can accept the 3-year term with 10% term discount and 50% upfront in cash.
- Milestone schedule may be aligned to product ramp (9 months and 21 months) — Redwood will include explicit deliverables that map to usage targets in the SOW.
- However, because Quantaflow is unable to provide an LC, Redwood requires either: (A) a small security deposit equal to 10% of total contract value held until final milestone clears, or (B) an intercompany guarantee from Quantaflow's parent. This is non-negotiable for Net 90 milestone invoices under the discounted pricing.

If neither option is acceptable, we can offer the same term with a reduced 7% discount or require Net 60 on milestones. Ben is copied to finalize payment language and schedule in the SOW.

Next steps: if you confirm (A) or (B) or accept 7% discount/Net 60, we'll generate a redline-ready SOW and payment schedule.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: QF-SOW-draft.pdf (pdf)
